  STRATEGY glycaemic_control_aggressive:
    description "Aggressive calorie deficit for weight loss with glycaemic control for PCOS. Monitor for under-fuelling, fatigue, and cycle disruption. Not recommended long-term."
    guidelines:

      - "Prioritize lean protein at every meal to preserve muscle mass"
      - "Emphasize high-fiber, low glycaemic index (GI) carbohydrates: oats, quinoa, brown rice, sweet potato, legumes, berries, apples, pears, non-starchy vegetables"
      - "Include healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish"
      - "Pair carbohydrates with protein and/or fat to slow glucose absorption"
      - "Limit added sugars and refined grains: avoid sugary drinks, pastries, white bread, white rice"
      - "Stay hydrated: aim for at least 2L water daily"
      - "Do not skip meals; spread calories across 3 meals and 1 snack"
      - "If experiencing fatigue, poor recovery, or cycle changes, increase calories"
      - "If training fasted, consume a balanced meal within 60 minutes post-workout"
      - "Monitor for signs of under-fuelling: dizziness, poor sleep, irritability, persistent soreness"
      - "Consult a registered dietitian for individualized support"

  STRATEGY glycaemic_control_aggressive:
    description "Aggressive calorie deficit for weight loss with glycaemic control for PCOS. Monitor for under-fuelling, fatigue, and cycle disruption. Not recommended long-term."
    guidelines:
      - "Reduce daily calorie intake by 25-30% below maintenance, but not below 1400 kcal/day unless medically supervised"
      - "Prioritize lean protein at every meal to preserve muscle mass"
      - "Emphasize high-fiber, low glycaemic index (GI) carbohydrates: oats, quinoa, brown rice, sweet potato, legumes, berries, apples, pears, non-starchy vegetables"
      - "Include healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish"
      - "Pair carbohydrates with protein and/or fat to slow glucose absorption"
      - "Limit added sugars and refined grains: avoid sugary drinks, pastries, white bread, white rice"
      - "Stay hydrated: aim for at least 2L water daily"
      - "Do not skip meals; spread calories across 3 meals and 1 snack"
      - "If experiencing fatigue, poor recovery, or cycle changes, increase calories"
      - "If training fasted, consume a balanced meal within 60 minutes post-workout"
      - "Monitor for signs of under-fuelling: dizziness, poor sleep, irritability, persistent soreness"
      - "Consult a registered dietitian for individualized support"

      snack: "Carrot sticks and hummus"
